directAnswer: St. Marcellus I was the thirtieth bishop of Rome, elected in 308 after a long vacancy that followed the Great Persecution. He tried to restore order and imposed penance on Christians who had lapsed, which provoked violent unrest in the Roman community. Emperor Maxentius exiled him, and he died in exile in January 309.

paras: When Marcellus was finally elected in 308, the Roman Church had been without a bishop for several years and its organization had been badly damaged. The Liber Pontificalis says he reorganized the city into twenty-five titles, or parish districts, for baptism, penance, and the burial of martyrs, though historians are unsure how much of this is accurate.

Some scholars once suggested that Marcellus and his predecessor Marcellinus were the same man, because their names and stories became confused in early lists, but most historians treat them as two different bishops.

sections.h2: Penance for the Lapsed and Exile Under Maxentius
paras: Many Christians had lapsed during the persecution and now sought readmission. Marcellus required them to do penance first. An epitaph composed for him later in the century by Pope Damasus says this stern policy angered the lapsed and led to discord, violence, and bloodshed, and that, because of the crime of one who had denied Christ, Marcellus was driven into exile by the tyrant, meaning Emperor Maxentius.

Marcellus died in exile in January 309. A later legend says he was forced to work in a stable set up in a church, which became the origin of the Church of San Marcello al Corso, but that story is not historical. He was buried in the Catacomb of Priscilla, and his feast is January 16.

keyFacts: Thirtieth bishop of Rome, May 27, 308, to January 16, 309
Elected after a vacancy of several years following the persecution
Required penance before readmitting lapsed Christians
Exiled by Emperor Maxentius; died in exile
Buried in the Catacomb of Priscilla; feast day January 16

faqs.question: Why was Pope Marcellus I exiled?
faqs.answer: His insistence that lapsed Christians do penance before readmission caused violent unrest in Rome. According to the epitaph by Pope Damasus, Emperor Maxentius exiled him to restore order.

faqs.question: Is the Church of San Marcello al Corso connected to Pope Marcellus I?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is dedicated to him. A legend says he was forced to tend animals in a stable at that site, but historians regard the story as unhistorical.
